The stage was set for a classic cup tie on September 8, 2026, as two sides hungry for progress faced off in the Carabao Cup . With knockout football on the line, the atmosphere was electric from the opening whistle as both tactical setups looked for a decisive edge. A First Half of Near Misses Sunderland started the brighter of the two sides, looking to use the width of the pitch to stretch the Hull City defense. Early on, Wilson Isidor found himself in a promising position following a Trai Hume cross, but his effort whistled past the post. The home side continued to pile on the pressure, with Jules Ahoka forcing a fine save from Dillon Phillips . The Hull City goalkeeper was kept busy throughout the opening period, notably denying Chemsdine Talbi with a sharp stop just before the break. Hull City were not without their moments, looking dangerous on the break through the pace of Mohamed-Ali Cho . The forward sent a warning shot from distance that narrowly missed the target, but for the most part, the visitors were forced to focus on their defensive duties. Despite several corners and half-chances for the hosts, the first half concluded without a goal, leaving the tactical battle wide open for the second period. Talbi Strikes to Decide the Tie The second half saw the intensity ramp up as both managers looked to their benches for inspiration. The introduction of Thomas Meunier provided the spark Sunderland needed. In the 71st minute, a swift counter-attack saw Meunier slide a perfectly weighted through ball to Chemsdine Talbi . From outside the box, Talbi unleashed a magnificent right-footed strike that flew into the top left corner, leaving Phillips with no chance and giving the home fans reason to celebrate. Hull City threw everything forward in the closing stages, searching desperately for an equalizer. Joe Gelhardt missed a golden opportunity from close range, and a flurry of late corners kept the Sunderland faithful on the edge of their seats. However, with Omar Alderete and Luke O'Nien holding firm at the back, the hosts navigated the five minutes of added time to secure their place in the next round, surviving a late scare from a resilient Hull side.

The double from the Norwegian striker left the visitors with a mountain to climb. As the clock ticked on, Palace manager made strategic changes, introducing Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton to freshen up the midfield. The impact was almost immediate. In the 72nd minute, Jørgen Strand Larsen turned provider, sliding a through ball to Daichi Kamada just outside the area. The Japanese international composed himself before unleashing a precise right-footed shot into the bottom left corner, effectively ending the contest as a spectacle. Professional Finish to Progress To their credit, Middlesbrough refused to go down without a fight. Late attempts from Will Lankshear and Rokas Pukstas kept the Palace defense on their toes, while Myles Peart-Harris received a yellow card as frustrations began to boil over. The Cherries continued to press forward, creating several scoring opportunities. Bafodé Diakité nearly doubled the lead with a header that was expertly saved by Lincoln City goalkeeper Joe Gauci , while Justin Kluivert and Álvaro Rodríguez remained constant threats in the final third throughout the first half. The persistence of the home side was rewarded in the 69th minute when Ryan Christie rose highest to meet a David Brooks cross following a corner, heading it firmly into the center of the goal. The Devon Derby returned to the Carabao Cup stage on August 10, 2026 , as Plymouth Argyle hosted Exeter City in a high-stakes encounter. Both teams sought to assert local dominance in a match that remained balanced and unpredictable until the very final moments of play. A Tense Exchange of Chances From the opening whistle, Plymouth Argyle looked to dictate the tempo, with Harvey White testing the waters early with a long-range effort. The home side continued to pile on the pressure as Ronan Curtis and Aribim Pepple forced Exeter City goalkeeper Jack Bycroft into several crucial saves. Despite the territorial advantage for the Pilgrims, Exeter remained dangerous on the break, with Charlie Cummins nearly finding the target from a set-piece situation that flew just over the bar. As the first half progressed, the physical nature of the derby became evident. Charlie Cummins received an early booking for a heavy challenge, signaling the intensity of the midfield battle. While Mathias Ross and Pepple continued to search for the breakthrough before the interval, the visitors’ defense held firm, ensuring the scoreline remained level at the break after a series of blocked attempts and narrow misses. Momentum Shifts and a Costly Red Card The second half saw Exeter City grow in confidence, creating a flurry of opportunities. Taylor Perry and Andrew Oluwabori both came close to silencing the home crowd, with the latter seeing a headed effort rise just too high. Plymouth's manager responded by introducing fresh legs, bringing on Matthew Sorinola and Julio Pleguezuelo to regain control of the flanks and revitalize an attack that was struggling to find a clinical edge. The game reached a turning point in the 87th minute when Ethan Sutherland , who had been cautioned only nine minutes earlier, committed a tactical foul that resulted in a second yellow card. His dismissal left Exeter City a man down for the closing stages, forcing them into a defensive shell as Plymouth Argyle launched a final, desperate assault on the Grecians' goal. Stoppage Time Fireworks Just as the match seemed destined for a penalty shootout, the deadlock was finally broken in the 92nd minute. A pinpoint corner from Harvey White found the head of Alex Hartridge , who powered his effort into the top left corner from close range. The breakthrough sent the home supporters into a frenzy, but the drama was far from over as the clock ticked deep into added time. With Exeter pushing everyone forward in search of an equalizer, Plymouth Argyle struck again in the 94th minute. Freddie Issaka spearheaded a lightning-fast counter-attack, squaring the ball to Aribim Pepple in the center of the box. Pepple made no mistake, slotting the ball home to secure a 2-0 victory. Although Josh Gordon forced one final save from Murphy Cooper in the dying seconds, the result was already sealed, sending Plymouth through to the next round.

On February 5, 2026 , two heavyweights of English football collided in a high-stakes Carabao Cup encounter. The atmosphere at the stadium was electric as both sides looked to secure their progression in a competition that has become a vital battlefield for silverware. A Dream Start and VAR Drama The match ignited within the opening sixty seconds. Arsenal wasted no time establishing dominance as Riccardo Calafiori found the back of the net with a clinical left-footed finish, following a sharp assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly . The goal was briefly held in the balance during a tense VAR review, but the referee eventually pointed to the center spot, confirming the lead. Manchester City struggled to find their rhythm early on, evidenced by Phil Foden receiving a yellow card for unsportsmanlike conduct as frustrations began to simmer. As the first half progressed, the visitors' tactical discipline kept the hosts at bay. The City midfield, usually so dominant in possession, found itself crowded out by a hungry Arsenal press that refused to let the game settle into a predictable pattern. Clinical Execution and Goal-Line Clearances The Gunners doubled their advantage in the 28th minute through a beautifully orchestrated team move. Martin Ødegaard provided the vision with a key pass to Christos Tzolis , who delivered a perfect cross for Kai Havertz to head home. The drama intensified ten minutes later when Riccardo Calafiori was booked for diving in the penalty box—a controversial decision that denied Arsenal a chance for a third from the spot. Late in the first half, both ends of the pitch saw incredible defensive heroics. Martin Ødegaard saw a certain goal hacked off the line, only for Jeremy Doku to experience the same frustration at the other end moments later. These narrow escapes kept the scoreline at 2-0 heading into the interval, leaving the door slightly ajar for a potential comeback. Ødegaard Seals the Deal Any hopes of a Manchester City recovery were effectively extinguished just three minutes after the restart. Martin Ødegaard , who had been the architect of so much of his team's success, turned scorer by finishing with his left foot after excellent work from Tzolis and Lewis-Skelly . The 3-0 deficit prompted Pep Guardiola to make sweeping changes, including replacing Erling Haaland with Omar Marmoush , but the momentum remained firmly with the North Londoners. Despite late pressure from Antoine Semenyo and creative sparks from Rayan Cherki , the Arsenal defense remained resolute. Gabriel and Piero Hincapie made crucial interventions to protect the clean sheet. In front of a crowd of 58,056 , the final whistle confirmed a comprehensive and deserved victory for the Gunners, as they marched into the next round with a performance of genuine authority.
